newsitem.title: UK: London plans huge dome for millennium exhibition.
newsitem.headline: London plans huge dome for millennium exhibition.

text.p: Britain plans to welcome the millennium with an exhibition aimed at attracting more than 12 million visitors and centred on what is described as the world's largest dome -- a kilometre (more than half-a-mile) round.

The year-long Millennium Exhibition, due to open on December 31, 1999, will be based on a 130-acre (50-hectare) site in the South London district of Greenwich -- home to the prime meridian or zero line of longitude, source of Greenwich Mean Time.
An application for permission for the exhibition was submitted to Greenwich local council on Thursday and 80,000 residents will be invited to give their views on the plans.

The application includes plans to create a park, gardens, a plaza and performance area and a variety of transport and parking facilities on the site near the River Thames. At present it is a wasteland with the remains of a gasworks.
The dome, made of translucent fabric, will be more than 50 metres (165 feet) high. It will be suspended from 12 masts and held in place by steel cable.
Its floor area of 80,000 square metres (860,000 sq ft) will be twice that of the Georgia Dome used during the Atlanta Olympics.
If granted planning permission, work on the project will start in mid-1997. The exhibition will open on December 31, 1999.

"There is still a long way to go, but potentially we could have the biggest and best in the world -- one which will create employment, improve a run-down area of our capital city and encourage new economic investment," said Barry Hartop, chief executive of the exhibition's organising company.
The exhibition is expected to cost about 500 million pounds ($815 million) to put on.
About 200 million pounds is expected to be provided by funds from the National Lottery but private companies have been reluctant to provide matching funds. ($1=.6141 Pound)
